claims.statement: Runner reimage selects from available GitHub-owned images then saves; no arbitrary custom-image support inferred or runner image changed.

Runner group removal selects intended group, Remove group, reviews confirmation then removes. Destructive procedure is source evidence, not authorization; dependent access/recovery must be separately reviewed.
Runner rename edits Name and saves; names can affect functionality in other sources, so no actual rename authorized.
Repository numeric ID is distinct from repository name; illustrative ID is not a real target identity.
Owner numeric account ID differs from owner name; illustrative value is not actual principal identity.
Available runner resize choices depend on installed image; select Size and Save is not capacity change approval or evidence of cost/performance.
The parent keyword allows several contexts via linked availability table; unspecified keyword and exact supported contexts require parent resolution.

Same-repository $/.github/workflows syntax is recommended but unavailable GHES; ./ syntax also allowed. External owner/repo path/ref permits FPT public/private and GHEC/GHES public/internal/private workflows.

External ref allows SHA/tag/branch, same-name tag wins, commit SHA safest. Local $/ or ./ uses caller commit; $/ forbids ref suffix and GHES use. refs/heads/tags prefixes and expressions/contexts disallowed in this calling keyword, distinct from access-policy ref syntax.
run_id uniquely identifies a run within repository and stays unchanged on rerun; attempt identity must be tracked separately.
run_number starts1 and increments per new run of a particular workflow, unchanged on rerun. It is workflow-scoped, not repository-wide unique or attempt counter.
Runner application is open source with upstream contribution/issue link; linked repository license/code are not audited here.
Runner architecture values are X86, X64, ARM or ARM64. Case and identity differ from arbitrary workflow labels; no actual hardware observed.
Runner debug marker exists only with debug logging and value1; absence is not an error or complete verbosity audit, and enabled logs may need sensitive-data review.
Runner environment differentiates github-hosted and self-hosted. Description is source schema, not actual isolation, ownership or trust verification.

GHEC data-residency runners require additional hostnames beyond this list. Essential operations require github.com, api.github.com and *.actions.githubusercontent.com; source list is not complete for every use case.

Action downloads use codeload.github.com; summaries/logs/artifacts/caches results-receiver.actions.githubusercontent.com and *.blob.core.windows.net; updates objects, objects-origin, github-releases and github-registry-files under githubusercontent.com.

OIDC uses *.actions.githubusercontent.com; packages/containers *.pkg.github.com, pkg-containers.githubusercontent.com and ghcr.io; Git LFS github-cloud.githubusercontent.com and github-cloud.s3.amazonaws.com. Categories don't authorize firewall writes.

FPT/GHEC Dependabot update jobs use dependabot-actions.githubapp.com; release assets release-assets.githubusercontent.com; VNET api.snapcraft.io and *.core.windows.net. Wildcards, CNAME follow-up and version context remain separately verified.

Repository access policy chooses selected or all repositories; default private-only can be overridden except organization group inherited from enterprise cannot override it. Configuration is not effective access proof.

GHEC/GHES workflow group access selects all or full owner/repository paths and cannot override enterprise-shared policy. Non-reusable pin branch, reusable branch/tag/full SHA; qualify ambiguous refs with refs/heads or refs/tags; only directly defined jobs access. This policy syntax differs from reusable calling syntax where such prefixes are forbidden.

Enterprise group creation navigation consists of four shared enterprise/policy/Actions/group includes plus New runner group and name input. Dependency bodies and actual create policy are separately scoped.
Enterprise runner-group navigation is four shared includes; reference presence is not full include-body review or authorized enterprise access.
Organization runner-group navigation opens organization Settings then shared Actions-group sidebar include. Neither target access nor included body is certified here.
